title: Release supply chain: SBOM, provenance, notices, reproducibility, and dependency review
objective: Make every Cotra release artifact verifiable and accountable without widening authority: ship third-party notices in the payload, produce a deterministic archive, a CycloneDX SBOM that reflects the actual shipped dependency graph, a provenance record and a free GitHub build-provenance attestation, test build reproducibility for real, audit dependencies for known vulnerabilities, record the dependency and license review, and validate installation from the archive itself.

include: scripts/third-party-notices.mjs generating THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt from the crates linked into the shipped binaries (normal edges, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc) and the packaged npm closure, with declared licenses and full shipped license texts, included in every release payload

scripts/archive-release.mjs producing a deterministic ZIP (sorted entries, fixed timestamps and attributes, fixed compression method and level, UTF-8 names, and no extra fields or comments) of the release directory
scripts/generate-sbom.mjs producing a deterministic CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM of the shipped crates, npm packages, and every payload file with SHA-256 digests and the dependency graph
scripts/provenance.mjs recording source revision, workflow run, toolchain versions, lock digests, artifact digests, SBOM digest, and the reproducibility result, observing only what is available
deterministic release build flags (deterministic linker timestamps and source path remapping) applied consistently in CI qualification and the release workflow

a CI release-candidate job that builds and packages twice from two separate checkouts with the release flags, compares the shipped binaries and the final archives, generates the SBOM, notices, and provenance, extracts the archive and qualifies installation, MCP operation, update, rollback, failed-update recovery, stop, and uninstall from the extracted archive, and uploads the candidate artifacts
a CI supply-chain job running npm audit on the locked production graph and cargo audit with a pinned cargo-audit version against the RustSec database
the release workflow attaching the archive, SBOM, provenance, notices, and SHA256SUMS to the draft release and creating a GitHub build-provenance attestation for the archive
docs/research/DEPENDENCY_LICENSE_REVIEW.md recording every shipped dependency's version, license, purpose, and security notes with the audit results, without claiming legal certainty
exclude: code signing with a paid certificate
any change to runtime behavior, MCP tools, capabilities, approvals, or lifecycle commands
claims of reproducibility beyond what the CI comparison observes
publishing a release or creating a tag

authority_delta.filesystem: None at runtime. Build scripts write only to their output directories.
authority_delta.network: None at runtime. CI fetches the RustSec advisory database and npm audit data; these are build-time checks on GitHub-hosted runners.
authority_delta.secrets: None. The attestation uses the workflow's OIDC token; no secret is added.

invariants: the SBOM and notices are generated from the actual shipped dependency graph and payload, not a hand-maintained list
the archive is byte-identical for identical release directories
reproducibility is reported exactly as observed by comparing independent builds
release artifacts are never published by automation; drafts only

acceptance.claim: CI builds and packages twice from separate checkouts with the release flags and reports, per shipped binary and for the final release archive, whether the SHA-256 digests match, with the result recorded in the provenance record.

CI produces a deterministic archive, a CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM covering every shipped crate, npm package, and payload file, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt with no component lacking a license, and a provenance record, and uploads them as release-candidate artifacts.
CI extracts the archive and qualifies installation, MCP operation, update, rollback, recovery, stop, and uninstall from the extracted archive.
CI runs npm audit and cargo audit and fails on any known vulnerability.
The release workflow attaches the archive, SBOM, provenance, notices, and SHA256SUMS to a draft release and creates a build-provenance attestation, and still never publishes.
The dependency and license review records every shipped dependency with version, license, purpose, and audit results.

All closed SG-000001 through SG-000044 regressions pass unchanged, and exact-head CI, genuine TypeSafe Jev, Alibaba Open Code Review, manual review of excluded files, and zero unresolved review threads all pass.

successor_requirements.p13_next: The threat-model regression and final quality grain completes the regression matrix, MCP exposure drift tests, dead-code removal, user documentation, and the final repository review before the P13 exit.

done_when: Release artifacts carry notices, a deterministic archive, a graph-accurate SBOM, provenance with an observed reproducibility result, a build-provenance attestation, and audited dependencies, with no runtime authority change.
